clue.text: Charlie wears floppy straw hat, Penny a bracelet

indicators.note: whatever wears clothing has it around it, so the next letters go round the first
something floppy has lost its shape, so these letters lose their order too

parts.note: taken as written
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet
p is the abbreviation for a penny

explanation.surface: Someone called Charlie dons a battered straw hat, and a girl called Penny wears a bracelet.
explanation.walkthrough: C goes inside the hat letters, the whole lot is shuffled, and P is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A watch strap goes round the wrist, so it is a band worn like a bracelet.

clue.text: Ace opportunity to find a bargain game installed, generally

explanation.walkthrough: 'Game installed' sounds like computer software being set up, but the game is a sport placed inside the bargain event.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean usually or in most cases, so the idiom swaps for the adverb.

clue.text: Leaders of Conservatives elected lovable Etonian Boris, a famous name

parts.note: the initial letter of each of these five words

explanation.definitionFit: A celeb is a celebrity, someone whose name is widely known, so a famous name stands for that person.

clue.text: Country boys love Niamh loads!

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the lads all adore a girl called Niamh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loads' reads as 'lots', an intensifier, but it is the verb: these words hold a cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: Slovenia is a nation in central Europe, bordering Italy, Austria, Hungary and Croatia.

clue.text: Wealthy individual acquiring Motor plc cooked books produced by her

parts.note: synonym

clue.text: Vesta's here, ready to provide illumination

explanation.walkthrough: Vesta was the Roman hearth goddess whose sacred fire burned constantly; Swan Vestas is a well-known British brand of matches.

clue.text: Miss an important part of school?

parts.words: Miss an important part of school?
parts.note: setter's reading: Miss as a title for a girl, the top senior pupil in a school

explanation.walkthrough: 'Miss' looks like a verb, to fail to attend; it is a noun, a young woman. In British schools this senior pupil is chosen to lead and represent the students.
explanation.definitionFit: The senior girl pupil chosen to represent a school is a young miss with an important role there.

clue.text: Policeman not working properly, time to replace force?
